claim: The published Bayesian ECI (code e04929a, data of 2026-11-13) is robust to its priors: under every prior in a pre-registered set of defensible alternatives, model scores, the frontier ranking and the 90% credible intervals move by less than would change any conclusion Epoch reports.
why_it_matters: The repository switched ECI to a Bayesian fit (merge commit e04929a, 2026-11-03) and Epoch reports 90% credible intervals, but publishes no prior sensitivity. Capabilities and difficulties have flat Uniform(-50, 50) priors, and 72 of 256 models have 6 or fewer scores. The newest frontier models, which carry the headline numbers, have few benchmarks still in the mid-range, so the priors on slopes and noise could matter most where readers look.
minimum_convincing_evidence: W2 reproduces the published scores and intervals; W3 shows the sensitivity metrics flag a deliberately strong prior; W5 runs the power-scaling screen and then scores every defensible prior of the full pre-registered grid against the C1 decision rule, with a seed-to-seed noise floor measured for every metric.
anti_claim: Apparent robustness is an artefact of perturbations too small to matter, or of metrics that average over the many dense models and hide shifts at the frontier and in sparse models.
falsifier: Any defensible prior P1-P10 in prior-grid.json for which, in the all-models or frontier stratum, S1 Spearman(ECI_k, ECI_0) < 0.99, or S2 more than 5% of non-anchor models shift by more than a quarter of their baseline 90% interval width, or S3 more than 5% have an interval-width ratio outside [0.8, 1.25], or S4 the top-10 set changes or a top-10 adjacent pair's P(i ranked above j) moves by 0.10 or more. Definitions in M1-M3.

decision_if_unproven.note: If every failure is in the sparse stratum only, restate C1 as robust for the 184 models with 7 or more scores (requires S1-S3 to pass in the dense stratum) and list the sparse models as prior-dependent. If the frontier or all-models stratum fails, C1 is false as stated: report which prior drives it. add_evidence does not apply to a failed rule because the data are fixed; it applies only to an unresolved grid entry (one more attempt) and to an S5-only flag (two exact power-scaled refits).

decision_rule: Quantities (M1): per-draw anchored ECI; point estimate = posterior mean; W = 95th minus 5th percentile. Baseline = fit P0 (default priors, W5 sampler settings, seed 12345). Strata (M2), fixed from the published files before any fit: all (256 models; 254 non-anchor models for S2, S3, S5); frontier (the 20 models with the highest published eci in eci_scores.csv, Claude Fable 5.2 down to GPT-5.5); sparse (the 72 models with 6 or fewer rows in the fit input). Dense (the 184 models with 7 or more rows, 182 non-anchor) is reported and is used only to state the narrowed claim. For each defensible prior k in P1-P10 and each stratum: S1 Spearman(ECI_k, ECI_0) >= 0.99 over the stratum's models; S2 share of non-anchor models with abs(ECI_k - ECI_0) > 0.25 x W_0 is <= 5% (at most 12 of 254, 1 of 20, 3 of 72); S3 share with W_k / W_0 outside [0.8, 1.25] is <= 5% (same counts); S4 (scored once, counted in the frontier and all-models strata) the set of the 10 highest posterior-mean ECI is unchanged and abs(P_k(i>j) - P_0(i>j)) < 0.10 for each of the 9 adjacent pairs of the baseline top-10 order. S5 (screen on the W2 seed-12345 draws, no refit, run first in W5): power-scaling sensitivity psens of the three hyperpriors <= 0.05 for at least 95% of non-anchor models' ECI in each stratum. Verdicts. Robust: all ten priors resolved, S1-S4 pass in all three strata, S5 passes. Conditionally robust: every S1-S3 failure is in the sparse stratum only and S4 passes. Sensitive: any S1-S4 failure in the all-models or frontier stratum. An S5-only flag does not decide the verdict: the two exact power-scaled refits of the flagged hyperprior (alpha 0.8 and 1.25, M3) are scored with S1-S4 as extra grid entries and they decide. An entry still unresolved after its retry means C1 cannot be Robust and is reported as not established for that prior. Added by the restructure of 2026-11-18 and exploratory, outside this rule: the reference-prior entry PR (W1) and the S5-targeted refits at alpha 0.5 and 2 are scored with S1-S4 and reported, but never enter the verdict.
loss_contract: Every grid entry is reported, including the stress priors X1 and X2 (reported, not scored), fits that fail convergence (counted as unresolved, never dropped), and the two anchor models (kept in S1 and S4, excluded from S2, S3 and S5 because their values are fixed by definition). The seed-to-seed noise floor of every metric (P0 against P0b) is reported next to each result. The exploratory entry PR and every S5-targeted refit are listed with the grid and labelled exploratory.
falsification_test: W5 refit grid scored against the decision rule; see falsifier.
selection_history: Before writing this plan we inspected: Epoch's code and README, the 2026-11-13 zip's benchmark list, per-model observation counts, published ECI and interval widths, and EEE collection names. No refit was run. The prior grid is written from the README's stated priors and the observation-count distribution.

Restructure of 2026-11-18 (nothing executed): B0-B3 were merged into block W (Revision Log R17-R25). No threshold, grid entry P1-P10, X1, X2 or rule of this claim was changed. The reference prior PR was chosen by a prior predictive simulation on the observed (model, benchmark) pattern only, with the published capability spread of the review in view; it is exploratory.

Review of 2026-11-13 (before any run): the reviewer read the published file eci_bootstraps.json (500 posterior draws per model and benchmark) to check that thresholds are attainable. Facts used: published means differ from the 500-draw means by up to 0.88 ECI points (0.053 x W), which sets the Monte Carlo tolerance in G0; published adjacent-pair probabilities in the top 10 range from 0.52 to 0.996; raw capability draws stay within abs 12.6, far from the +/-50 bounds; the across-model SD of raw capability means is 2.62. No prior in the grid was added, removed or re-centred using these numbers.
predecessor_failures: Our own v1 composite model: full NUTS did not converge on the 45k-observation fitting set and we fell back to SVI. Carry forward: ECI's 2,879 observations are 15x fewer and Epoch's sampler uses a dense mass matrix, but W2 must confirm convergence before any sensitivity number is trusted.

claim: The ECI's Beta-IRT model is adequate for Epoch's data: checks with simulation-calibrated p-values find no structural misfit (dimensionality, item-curve shape, dispersion, time drift or developer-specific effects) large enough to bias ECI scores, and held-out 90% predictive intervals cover at their nominal rate.
why_it_matters: Epoch's repo ships a diagnostic suite (per-benchmark and pooled posterior predictive p-values for nine marginal statistics, in-sample and PSIS-LOO PIT calibration and coverage, PSIS-LOO), but the ECI page publishes no results from it, and marginal score statistics have little power against the misfits that matter for a one-dimensional index: a second skill dimension, benchmark-specific contamination, or developer-specific over-performance.
minimum_convincing_evidence: Epoch's own suite run and reported (W4a); the structural checks T1-T7 referred to 199 null simulations with refits and shown in W3 to detect planted misfit (W4b); 5-fold held-out coverage (W4c).
anti_claim: A clean result reflects checks with no power (posterior predictive p-values are conservative because the data are used twice), not an adequate model.
falsifier: The Inadequate verdict of the decision rule: a check with max-T adjusted p < 0.01, or overall held-out 90% coverage outside [0.85, 0.95], or a benchmark with 20 or more held-out scores whose coverage fails the Bonferroni binomial test, where the failure is not localised to at most 10 benchmarks or removing those benchmarks (W4d) moves a model by more than 0.25 x W_0.

decision_if_unproven.note: Report the misfit as a finding: which check fails, on which benchmarks or developers, and the size of the ECI shift when the offending benchmarks are dropped (W4d). The claim becomes 'ECI is adequate except for X, which moves scores by Y'.

decision_rule: T1-T7 (M5) are scalar discrepancy statistics, larger meaning worse fit, computed the same way on the real data with the W2 fit and on each of R = 199 G-null datasets with its own refit. Unadjusted p_k = (1 + number of converged null replicates with T_k >= observed T_k) / (R' + 1). Family-wise adjusted p_k by single-step max-T over the seven checks on standardised log statistics (M6). A check is rejected if adjusted p_k < 0.01; with R' = 199 the smallest attainable value is 0.005. Held-out coverage (M7): the share of the 2,704 held-out scores whose PIT lies in [0.05, 0.95] must be in [0.85, 0.95]; each of the 44 benchmarks with 20 or more held-out scores is flagged if an exact two-sided binomial test of coverage = 0.90 gives p < 0.01 / 44. Adequate: no check rejected, overall coverage in range, no benchmark flagged; the statement is limited to misfit types whose targeted check reached power >= 0.8 in W3, and the others are listed as not assessed. Adequate with exceptions: every rejection or flag is localised (M6) to a benchmark set F with at most 10 members, and the W4d refit without F moves no retained non-anchor model by more than 0.25 x W_0 and drops no frontier model. Inadequate: any other rejection or coverage failure. Inconclusive: nothing rejected, but neither T2 (on G-2D) nor T5 (on G-offset) reached power 0.8; C2 then stays exploratory. The model expansions of W6 are exploratory, are fitted after this verdict is recorded and frozen, and never change it.
loss_contract: All seven checks are reported with unadjusted, adjusted and raw in-sample posterior predictive p-values; no check is dropped after seeing results. Non-converged null replicates are excluded from the reference set and counted. Scores at 0 or 1 are clipped to [0.001, 0.999] exactly as the likelihood sees them; Epoch's min and max statistics are excluded as Epoch excludes them.
falsification_test: W4 checks and held-out coverage against the decision rule; see falsifier.
selection_history: No posterior or residual was inspected before the check list T1-T7 was written.

Restructure of 2026-11-18 (nothing executed): B1 and B3 became W3 and W4; T1-T7, M5-M7, thresholds and the decision rule are unchanged. The G-null refits now also serve as SBC replicates (W3), which adds a report and no gate.

Review of 2026-11-13 (before any run): the scalar statistics, the max-T adjustment, the binomial coverage rule and three extra misfit generators were fixed from the observation pattern only (benchmark sizes, shared-model counts, organisation counts). No residual was computed.
predecessor_failures: Our v1 composite model failed its local-dependence kill test (Q3) on EEE data. Not inherited by ECI, but it is why T2 (residual correlation) is in the check list and why its threshold is pre-registered.

claim: ECI's posterior predictive intervals transfer to independently sourced scores: for model x benchmark pairs that EEE holds from a different source than Epoch, the ECI 90% predictive interval covers the EEE score at close to the nominal rate once EEE's own between-source spread is accounted for.
why_it_matters: The ECI intervals describe Epoch's own scores. Readers use them as statements about a model's capability, which only holds if they also predict scores obtained elsewhere. EEE is the one place where independent re-runs of the same benchmarks sit in a common schema.
minimum_convincing_evidence: An audited crosswalk (B4a) with a same-upstream positive control that matches near-exactly; coverage on independent pairs with a bootstrap interval; and the EEE-vs-EEE agreement rate on the same benchmarks as the noise floor.
anti_claim: Low coverage is caused by crosswalk errors (wrong model or benchmark version) or by differences in evaluation setup that any single-source index would suffer, not by ECI.
falsifier: Coverage of the 90% predictive interval on independent pairs below 0.65 while the EEE-vs-EEE agreement rate on the same benchmarks is estimable and at least 0.80, with the audit and same-upstream preconditions met.

decision_if_unproven.note: If coverage is low but EEE-vs-EEE agreement is equally low, the comparison cannot separate ECI from evaluation-setup variance: restrict to pairs whose EEE source matches Epoch's evaluation settings and report the result as `harness-limited`.

decision_rule: Coverage = share of matched independent pairs (M9) whose normalised EEE score has PIT in [0.05, 0.95] under the ECI predictive distribution (M8; PSIS-LOO weighted when Epoch's own score for the pair is in the fit). Agreement = share of independent source pairs for the same model and benchmark whose normalised scores differ by at most sqrt(2) x half the width of the ECI 90% predictive interval (nominal 0.90 if both were draws from the ECI predictive). Preconditions: audit finds at most 2 errors in 50 pairs; same-upstream median absolute difference <= 0.02; at least 100 independent pairs over at least 20 model groups and 5 benchmarks, else C3 is 'not assessed'. Verdicts: if agreement is estimable (30 or more source pairs) and below 0.80, the verdict is `harness-limited` whatever the coverage. Otherwise transfers if coverage >= 0.80; partial if 0.65 <= coverage < 0.80; does not transfer if coverage < 0.65. 'Does not transfer' falsifies C3 only when agreement is estimable and >= 0.80; if agreement is not estimable the result is reported as 'low coverage, noise floor unknown'. Verdicts use the point estimate; the 90% cluster-bootstrap interval is reported beside it. The verdict is defined on Epoch's base model as published (the W2 fit). Coverage under the adequate expansions of W6 is reported beside it as exploratory and never replaces it.
loss_contract: Every candidate EEE result is kept in the accounting with one class: matched-independent, matched-same-upstream, upstream-unknown, ambiguous-model, model-unmapped, model-not-in-fit, benchmark-not-in-fit, version-mismatch, metric-mismatch, duplicate. Classes are decided from metadata before any ECI prediction is computed.
falsification_test: B4b coverage against the decision rule; see falsifier.
selection_history: We looked at EEE collection names and source_metadata for 12 sampled records to judge independence (Arcadia inspect_ai, Writer wasp, UK AISI and Scale SEAL run their own evaluations; ARC Prize, Terminal-Bench and Mercor APEX are the same upstream Epoch cites). No scores were compared.

Review of 2026-11-13: llm-stats 'first_party' records relay developer-reported scores, so they are same-upstream wherever Epoch's source for that row is the developer's own report; the earlier note called them independent without that condition. The class is now decided per pair by the rule in M9.
predecessor_failures: Our v1 composite model reached only 0.70 coverage on its cross-source mask against a 0.85-0.95 target. C3 tests whether ECI shares that failure; the same EEE source offsets are the main suspect for both.
